findings.issue_text: [BUG] get_merged_pr_single_issue_template calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title), but _truncate_title is defined on CommitContextIntegration in this same diff, not on PRCommentWorkflow, so building a merged-PR comment raises AttributeError: type object 'PRCommentWorkflow' has no attribute '_truncate_title'. Every merged-PR comment generated by the GitHub/GitLab integrations fails with an AttributeError inside the comment-posting task, so the merged-PR issue-list comment feature is completely broken (the helper was added to the wrong class; nothing in the diff removes or adds _truncate_title on PRCommentWorkflow).

[BUG] GitHubPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body invokes self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...) and self.get_environment_info(...), but this diff defines both methods only on CommitContextIntegration, not on the PRCommentWorkflow base class that GitHubPRCommentWorkflow extends, so the workflow instance has no such attributes. Generating the merged-PR comment body raises AttributeError and the comment is never posted for any merged PR with linked issues; the pre-existing helpers the old code called via self. (format_comment_url/referrer_id) live on the workflow, so these new self.-calls resolve to nothing.

[BUG] GitlabPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body invokes self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...) and self.get_environment_info(...), methods this diff defines only on CommitContextIntegration and not on PRCommentWorkflow, so the workflow instance has no such attributes. Generating the merged-PR comment body raises AttributeError and the GitLab PR comment is never posted for any merged PR with linked issues.

[BUG] BrowserReportSerializer subclasses serializers.Serializer[Any]; DRF's Serializer does not implement __class_getitem__, so evaluating this base at class-definition time raises TypeError: 'type' object is not subscriptable when the module is imported. The URLconf import chain fails at web-service boot, so the collector endpoint (and every route in the same urls module) never loads; the service cannot start with this file present.

[BUG] Both gutted migrations (0917 and 0920, which carries the identical comment) defer the entire saved-search conversion to 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py, a file this diff never creates — the path-ordered diff goes straight from migrations/0920 to options/defaults.py. No deployment ever converts organization saved searches into GroupSearchView rows: the org saved-searches-to-views data migration silently never runs, so the feature the conversion supports has no backfilled data on upgrades or fresh installs.

[BUG] fetch_error_details zips error_ids against nodestore.backend.get_multi(...).values(), but nodestore's get_multi omits nodes that are missing instead of returning None placeholders, so any missing event shifts every subsequent error_id onto the wrong event's data (the 'if data is not None' guard is dead because get_multi never yields None). When any of a replay's error events has been dropped/expired from nodestore, each later error_id is paired with the preceding event's title/message, sending factually wrong error data to the Seer summarization request and producing summaries that cite errors the user's replay never produced.

[ADVISORY] The Snuba query_replay_instance call runs unconditionally on every GET and its result is used only to derive error_ids, so requests that pass enable_error_context=false still pay the full Snuba query before the flag is even evaluated. The opt-out added in this diff does not remove the new per-request Snuba load: every summarize-breadcrumbs request hits Snuba even when the caller explicitly disabled error context, adding query load on a path that previously only read segment metadata.

[ADVISORY] The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion checks use truthiness (self.initial_data.get('age')) and both fields are required=False, so a report containing neither age nor timestamp — or both set to 0 — passes validation. Malformed browser reports that violate the Reporting API's exactly-one-of requirement are accepted with a 200 and counted in the browser_reporting.raw_report_received metric, polluting the telemetry this endpoint was built to measure.

[ADVISORY] Removing the isinstance branch leaves the module-level _handle_regex_match helper with no remaining callers, while ParameterizationRegex (still exported in __all__) retains a run() callback contract nothing in the module now satisfies. The next change to the parameterization pipeline has to reason about a regex-callback path that can never execute, and the surviving ParameterizationRegex export invites configs that would now receive _incr_counter where a match-callback is expected.

[ADVISORY] gen_request_data drains the entire error_events list in its trailing while-loop on every page, so errors that fall after a page's last segment are re-emitted at the start of every subsequent page's output. Any consumer reading more than the first page of this paginated endpoint gets duplicate error lines in the logs sent to Seer for summarization, skewing the summary input toward repeated errors.

[BUG] BrowserReportSerializer requires `attempts` and `destination` and rejects `attempts=0` (min_value=1), but the W3C Reporting API wire format browsers actually deliver carries only age/body/type/url/user_agent with the attempts counter initialized to 0, so every real browser report fails validation. With issues.browser_reporting.collector_endpoint_enabled enabled, the collector returns 422 for every report a browser sends (the browser retries a few times, then discards the report), so the endpoint collects zero reports despite this validation rewrite whose purpose was to make ingestion correct.

[BUG] url = serializers.URLField() applies Django's URLValidator, which rejects opaque/non-hierarchical URLs such as `about:blank` or `blob:` URLs that browsers legitimately place in reports, whereas the removed dataclass accepted any string. Reports originating from blank iframes, error pages, or blob-backed documents are rejected with 422 and silently dropped, so crash/deprecation reports for those pages never reach Sentry.

[BUG] validate_timestamp and validate_age test the sibling field with a truthiness check (`if self.initial_data.get("age")`), so a payload containing both `age: 0` and `timestamp` (or `timestamp: 0` with `age`) passes validation even though the error messages declare the two fields mutually exclusive. Malformed reports violating the age/timestamp mutual-exclusion invariant are accepted whenever the co-present value is 0 (a valid, common age value), so the new validation does not enforce the rule it was added for.

[ADVISORY] The `enable_error_context=false` opt-out is evaluated only after `query_replay_instance` has already executed, so disabling error fetching still runs the full ClickHouse replay-instance query and process_raw_response. Clients that disable error context (and every request where error_ids ends up empty) still pay the Snuba query cost on every GET, adding avoidable ClickHouse load on the summarize endpoint.

[ADVISORY] error_events is bound once per request via functools.partial into analyze_recording_segments, and gen_request_data resets error_idx to 0 on each invocation, so every paginated page's Seer request receives the replay's entire error list rather than the errors in that page's segment range. For replays with more segments than one page, each page's summary re-includes all errors from earlier pages (emitted at the start of that page's log), duplicating error context across Seer requests and misattributing errors to the wrong segment range.

[ADVISORY] generate_error_log_message builds "User experienced an error: '{title}: {message}'" from nodestore data keys `title` and `message`, but nodestore event payloads for exception-only events carry neither a computed `title` nor a top-level `message`, producing lines like "User experienced an error: ': ' at 1730000000.0". A large class of error events contributes empty, information-free lines to the Seer prompt, degrading the breadcrumb summary this feature exists to improve.

[BUG] Replacing FlexCenter (which carried theme.overflowEllipsis, i.e. overflow:hidden) with plain `<Flex align="center">` removes the overflow that made the grid item's automatic minimum size zero, so the 1fr column of StyledPanelTable now sizes to the nowrap Name content. Long attachment names no longer ellipsize and instead expand the first grid column, overflowing the attachments panel horizontally.

[ADVISORY] The autofix automation tuning default now lives in two independently hardcoded places — DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT = "off" in src/sentry/constants.py:724 and register(key="sentry:autofix_automation_tuning", default="off") here — with nothing tying the two together. The next default change applied to one file but not the other silently diverges behavior between code paths that read the constant and paths that read the option registry default.

[ADVISORY] Owner-resolution logic (is_user/is_team branching writing owner_user_id/owner_team_id) is duplicated between update() (lines 66-79) and create() (lines ~123-131) with different shapes — update clears the opposite field inside each branch while create pre-initializes both to None. A future change to actor handling (new actor type, validation rule) must be applied in two places in the same file; editing only one leaves create and update behaving differently for the same owner payload.

[BUG] The only visible hunk traceable to the PR's stated intent ('Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System') is this null-segment guard in the replay delete path; every other visible hunk modifies unrelated subsystems, so the stated deliverable is not represented in the reviewable diff. The PR cannot be reviewed, tested, or reverted as a bulk-delete change: roughly 15 unrelated work streams (autofix defaults, data migrations, browser-report validation, PR-comment format, detector ownership, frontend refactors) ship under a replays title, so owning teams never review their changes and a revert of the replays work drags all of them with it.

[BUG] Adds a snuba-metrics dev service, four subscription-results Kafka consumers, a 'tracing' devservice profile listing ~19 services, and matching program entries (lines 131-141, 157-179, 325-332) — dev-environment work untraceable to replays bulk delete. Developers enabling the tracing profile now boot metrics and subscription-results consumers unrelated to this PR's purpose, and the devservices change lands without review from the metrics/subscription-results owners.

[BUG] Flips DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT from 'low' to 'off', with the twin default at src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py:205 — a product-default behavior change untraceable to replays bulk delete. Projects that never set sentry:autofix_automation_tuning silently stop running automatic autofix, a Seer-facing product change attributed in git history and release notes to a replays PR and reviewed by no Seer/ML owner.

[BUG] Rewrites the feedback-summary LLM prompt (55-word cap, theme-prioritization instructions) and changes the feedback join from '- {msg}' to a '------' delimiter — AI-prompt tuning untraceable to replays bulk delete. User-feedback summary output changes shape for all organizations with no review from the feedback feature owners; a summary-quality regression bisects to a replays commit.

[BUG] Deletes ParameterizationRegexExperiment, drops it from __all__ and the ParameterizationExperiment union (line 268), simplifies the experiment loop, and removes the registered option 'grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent' (src/sentry/options/defaults.py:2624-2628) — grouping cleanup untraceable to replays bulk delete. Any code still importing ParameterizationRegexExperiment fails at import time and any deployment with the traceparent option set loses its registration, all landing without review from the grouping owners inside a replays PR.

[BUG] Sets processing_deadline_duration on schedule_webhook_delivery (30s), drain_mailbox (300s, line 161), drain_mailbox_parallel (120s, line 239), and check_auth_identities (src/sentry/tasks/auth/check_auth.py:76-78) — taskworker tuning untraceable to replays bulk delete. Production webhook-delivery and auth-identity task timeouts change with no connection to the stated replays work, so a misjudged deadline is attributed to and reverted with the replays change.

[BUG] Introduces shared merged-PR comment rendering with 50-char title truncation and an environment suffix, rewiring the GitHub (src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:403-411) and GitLab (src/sentry/integrations/gitlab/integration.py:251-259) comment bodies — user-visible integration changes untraceable to replays bulk delete. Every merged-PR bot comment changes format (bullet '-' to '*', plain title+subtitle to a markdown-linked truncated title, appended ' in `env`'), landing without review or changelog attribution from the integrations owners.

[BUG] Replaces the permissive dataclass parse with a strict BrowserReportSerializer (ChoiceField on type, URLField, attempts min_value=1, age/timestamp mutual exclusion) plus per-report 422 error bodies (lines 101-130) — an endpoint contract change untraceable to replays bulk delete. Browser reports whose type is outside the eight hardcoded strings were previously accepted (the Literal was typing-only) and are now rejected with 422, changing ingestion behavior of a live browser-facing endpoint inside a PR where the issues owner has no review signal.

[BUG] Adds noise_config = NoiseConfig(ignore_limit=5) to DBQueryInjectionVulnerabilityGroupType — issue-noise behavior tuning untraceable to replays bulk delete. Suppression/escalation thresholds for DB query injection issues change for every project using the type, a security-alerting behavior change landing unreviewed under a replays title.

[BUG] Replaces the 0917 data-migration body with a no-op deferring to a 0921 'rerevised' migration, and identically guts 0920_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_revised.py:10-14 — saved-search migration rework untraceable to replays bulk delete. Conversion of organization saved searches to views now hinges entirely on the referenced 0921 migration rather than the code in these migrations, and the data-migration change ships without review from the settings/search owners inside a replays PR.

[BUG] Adds a new PreprodArtifactApiAssembleEvent (src/sentry/preprod/analytics.py:1-14, exported via src/sentry/preprod/__init__.py:1) and records it in the assemble endpoint before the feature-flag check — preprod instrumentation untraceable to replays bulk delete. preprod_artifact.api.assemble analytics fire for every POST, including requests from organizations without the preprod-artifact-assemble feature, polluting the metric and landing preprod work inside a replays PR.

[BUG] Adds error-context fetching to the summarize-breadcrumbs endpoint (Snuba query_replay_instance, nodestore get_multi, error/breadcrumb interleaving for the Seer prompt) — a new replay-summarization feature untraceable to the stated 'Self-Serve Bulk Delete System' intent. The endpoint gains two new remote calls per request and new response content, shipping under a bulk-delete title so replay-summarization stakeholders have no review signal and the feature's provenance is misattributed.

[BUG] Adds an equations passthrough parameter to run_top_events_timeseries_query and forwards it to the RPC (line 170) — logs-query capability work untraceable to replays bulk delete. The ourlogs query surface expands for an unrelated feature and lands without review from the search/execution owners inside a replays-attributed commit.

[BUG] Adds an owner ActorField to the detector validator (line 37) and owner_user_id/owner_team_id assignment in both update (lines 65-80) and create (lines 119-135) — new workflow-engine API capability untraceable to replays bulk delete. The detector API gains a writable ownership surface that changes who owns detectors created or edited through it, landing without review from the workflow-engine owners and mis-attributed to replays.

[BUG] Hoists get_slow_conditions_for_groups into process_delayed_workflows, adds a no-slow-conditions info log, fixes the event_data log key (line 583), and swaps workflow.py's logger to log_context.get_logger (src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/workflow.py:35) — processor refactoring untraceable to replays bulk delete. The delayed-workflow processing path is restructured with new logging and lands unreviewed by workflow-engine owners, so any regression in workflow notification timing bisects to the wrong feature.

[BUG] Mechanically replaces styled flex spacer/container components with the Flex component across codeSnippet.tsx, four codecov selector components (branchSelector, dateSelector, integratedOrgSelector, repoSelector), eventAttachments.tsx, and newTraceDetailsHeader.tsx — frontend cleanup untraceable to replays bulk delete. Six-plus UI files are restructured with no requirement from the stated intent, burying the replays changes in the diff and attributing any layout regression to the replays feature.

[BUG] Removes the 'Type' tooltip rows from every grouping-variant case and changes the chonk button press transition from 0.1s to 0.06s (static/app/components/core/button/styles.chonk.tsx:113) — user-visible UI changes untraceable to replays bulk delete. Users lose the tooltips explaining component/custom-fingerprint/built-in-fingerprint/performance variants in the grouping panel and button animation timing changes app-wide, both landing without attribution to their owning teams.

[BUG] gen_request_data resets error_idx to 0 on every invocation while analyze_recording_segments is bound via functools.partial(analyze_recording_segments, error_events) as on_results and therefore runs once per page with the same full replay-wide error_events list, and the trailing flush loop re-emits every unconsumed error at the end of each page. Any paginated summarize request (segments beyond one page) sends duplicated and out-of-order error entries to Seer: page N re-includes the errors already flushed at the end of page N-1 and errors belonging to later segments, inflating Seer payloads and skewing each page's summary with error context that does not belong to that page's time range.

[BUG] get() now calls query_replay_instance with no exception handling, adding a hard Snuba dependency to an endpoint that previously touched only object storage, while the nodestore call below it (fetch_error_details) deliberately degrades via try/except. During a Snuba outage or query timeout the summarize endpoint returns 500 for every caller even though breadcrumbs are fully servable from storage; the error-context feature takes the whole endpoint down instead of degrading to breadcrumbs-only the way the nodestore path already does.

[ADVISORY] The server's required error_ids data is projected through the client-controlled field list (fields=request.query_params.getlist("field") drives process_raw_response's row projection) and then read from response[0].get("error_ids"), so error context is produced only when the caller happens to pass field=error_ids. Any caller — or a frontend regression — that omits field=error_ids or passes a different field set silently gets breadcrumbs-only summaries with no error context and no signal that the feature no-op'd; the server should request the column it depends on itself rather than delegating its own query projection to the client.

[ADVISORY] The Snuba replay query and process_raw_response run before the enable_error_context check, so their results are computed and then discarded whenever error context is disabled. Every summarize request carrying enable_error_context=false pays a full Snuba query whose only consumer (error_ids) is thrown away, adding wasted Snuba load on the exact path callers use to avoid extra work.

[ADVISORY] fetch_error_details pairs error_ids with events.values() positionally via zip instead of looking nodes up by key, so the id-to-data mapping is only correct while get_multi returns every requested key in request order. If error_ids ever contains a duplicate id (collapsing dict keys and shortening values()) or a nodestore backend omits missing keys, every subsequent id silently pairs with the wrong event's title/message, feeding misattributed error text into the Seer summary prompt; a keyed lookup (events[node_id]) removes the ordering assumption.

[BUG] Both age and timestamp are declared required=False and neither validate_timestamp nor validate_age runs when both are absent, so a report containing neither field passes validation although both supported Reporting API specs require one of them. Malformed or hostile clients (the endpoint is CSRF-exempt and CORS-open) receive 200s for reports neither spec can produce, and the raw_report_received metric counts garbage as if it were real browser telemetry.

[BUG] The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion checks test truthiness (self.initial_data.get("age") / self.initial_data.get("timestamp")) instead of key presence, so a report carrying both timestamp and age=0 (or age with timestamp=0) validates despite the contract the docstrings state. Contradictory reports that the validators explicitly promise to reject are accepted and counted; the exclusion invariant only holds for truthy values, so the enforcement is weaker than the documented contract.

[BUG] url is now serializers.URLField(), whose validator only accepts http/https/ftp/ftps URLs with a // authority, replacing the previous accept-anything str field with no allowance for the non-http document URIs the Reporting API permits. Real reports with non-http document URLs — e.g. CSP-violation reports from about:blank/data: sandboxed frames or extension/error pages — now fail validation and return 422, silently dropping them from the browser_reporting metrics this endpoint exists to collect.

[BUG] update() reads validated_data.get("detector_type", instance.group_type) but the serializer's field is type (create() reads validated_data["type"]), so the detector_type key is never present and every update re-assigns instance.type from the existing group_type. PATCH requests that attempt to change a detector's type return 200 while the type is silently left unchanged — the caller's edit is dropped without any error, and the two methods bind two different names for the same validated_data key.

[ADVISORY] The owner-resolution logic (is_user/is_team branching into owner_user_id/owner_team_id) is duplicated between create() and update() with already-divergent shapes: update() explicitly clears the opposite field in each branch while create() relies on None initialization. The next owner-rule change (e.g. restricting owners to teams) must be applied in two structurally different blocks; a fix landed in one silently misses the other, and the divergence visible today shows this drift has already started.

[ADVISORY] CommitContextIntegration.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template reaches into PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title, coupling the integration base class to the comment-workflow class hierarchy for a helper that belongs beside ISSUE_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH and the template constant it serves. Title-truncation policy now lives in one class while its constant and its only new caller live in another, so the next truncation change must touch two layers — and the cross-class reference is a latent NameError if the module graph between integrations and the workflow classes changes.

[ADVISORY] Removing the regex-experiment branch leaves the module-level _handle_regex_match helper with no remaining caller in the dispatcher, while the ParameterizationRegex base class it was written for still exists with its different callback contract. The next editor sees two live-looking callback contracts (the dead re.Match helper and the active (str, int) counter) and can bind the wrong one when touching this dispatcher; the orphaned helper should be deleted together with the experiment class it served.

[ADVISORY] The new processing_deadline_duration values (30 here, 300 on drain_mailbox at ~line 161, 120 on drain_mailbox_parallel at ~line 239) are bare literals with no stated unit rationale or provenance, and drain_mailbox performs external HTTP deliveries whose duration directly determines whether the deadline fires. A drain_mailbox batch that outlives its deadline is killed and redelivered, which controls whether already-delivered webhooks get re-sent to customer endpoints — a tradeoff reviewers cannot evaluate because nothing records why 300/120/30 were chosen, and the next editor tuning one value has no reference for the others.

[ADVISORY] processing_deadline_duration=60 is a bare literal with no stated provenance on the check_auth_identities sweep task. If the identity sweep's worst-case duration exceeds 60s the task is killed and redelivered mid-sweep, reprocessing identities; nothing in the code records why 60 is safe for a sweep whose input size grows with the auth-identity table.

[ADVISORY] analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble") fires before the organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble feature check and before any request-body validation. Requests that are subsequently rejected with 404 (feature disabled) or 4xx (invalid payload) are counted as assemble events, so anyone reading this analytics stream to measure feature adoption or API usage gets inflated numbers that include rejected traffic.

[ADVISORY] DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT flips "low" to "off" in lockstep with the second copy of the same default in projectoptions/defaults.py (sentry:autofix_automation_tuning, line 205), silently changing effective behavior for every organization without an explicit option value. Existing organizations that relied on the default "low" autofix automation stop getting automatic Seer fixes with no migration or announcement accompanying the flip; the default is now maintained in two files that must be kept in sync manually, and this diff is the proof that every change requires touching both.

[BUG] This PR flips the shipped default for automatic autofix from 'low' to 'off' in two hand-edited places (DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT here and the register(key='sentry:autofix_automation_tuning', default='off') call in src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py:205), a fleet-wide product-behavior change with no connection to the PR's stated replays-bulk-delete objective. Every project that has not explicitly set sentry:autofix_automation_tuning — including existing projects reading the default at runtime — silently stops running automatic autofix; the previously shipped 'low' rollout behavior disappears fleet-wide and adoption/rollout metrics regress unless a human explicitly accepted this objective change, which the diff gives no evidence of.

[ADVISORY] Report handling changed from per-report counting to all-or-nothing validation: the loop returns 422 on the first invalid report before any metrics.incr runs, so valid reports sharing a payload with one invalid report are no longer counted at all (the old loop counted each report as it parsed it). Sentry's browser-reporting metrics undercount whenever a browser sends a batch containing any malformed report; per the Reporting API the browser re-sends the batch, so a deterministically-invalid report poisons every retry until the attempt limit is reached, permanently discarding the counts of the valid reports in those batches.

[ADVISORY] The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion check uses truthiness on initial_data and only runs when a field is present, so a report carrying neither age nor timestamp validates successfully, and a report with timestamp plus age=0 (or age plus timestamp=0) bypasses the exclusion check these validators exist to enforce. Reports that satisfy neither W3C draft (no age and no timestamp) are accepted and counted, and spec-violating reports carrying both fields with a 0 value slip through, polluting exactly the browser-reporting dataset this rewrite was meant to tighten.

[ADVISORY] The snuba query_replay_instance call that produces error_ids runs unconditionally before the enable_error_context check, so the disable flag only skips the nodestore fetch and never avoids the remote query it exists to turn off. Callers that pass enable_error_context=false to avoid the error-context cost still pay a full snuba query on every summarize request, so the opt-out knob added for cost control does not control the dominant added cost on this path.

[ADVISORY] Error-context extraction is coupled to client-supplied query parameters: process_raw_response filters rows to request.query_params.getlist('field'), so error_ids is empty unless the caller explicitly includes field=error_ids, and the new feature silently no-ops otherwise. Any summarize caller whose field list omits error_ids (older frontend builds during deploy skew, API consumers) gets summaries with no error context and no error or log explaining why, making the capability appear randomly broken instead of failing loudly.

[ADVISORY] fetch_error_details and gen_request_data inject every error of the replay into the Seer prompt with no cap on error_ids — a replay with hundreds of errors produces hundreds of nodestore fetches and an unbounded list of 'User experienced an error: ...' lines in the LLM request. Error-heavy replays drive per-request nodestore/snuba cost and Seer prompt size with no ceiling; an oversized Seer request surfaces as response.raise_for_status() raising inside on_results, turning the summarize request into a 500 for exactly the replays with the most errors.

[ADVISORY] MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE ends with a literal \n while both the GitHub and GitLab call sites still assemble the list with "\n".join(...), producing a blank line between every issue entry plus a trailing blank line, where the previous template produced a single-spaced list. Merged-PR comments posted to GitHub and GitLab render as a double-spaced issue list with a trailing empty line — a user-visible formatting regression introduced incidentally by the template move rather than a deliberate layout change.

[ADVISORY] analytics.record('preprod_artifact.api.assemble', ...) fires at the top of post() before the organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble feature check, so requests that are immediately rejected with 403 are recorded as assemble API usage. Adoption and funnel metrics for the preprod assemble API are inflated by denied traffic from organizations that never had the feature, skewing the product decisions this analytics event is meant to inform.

[ADVISORY] The autofix automation default exists as two hand-synced literals — register(key='sentry:autofix_automation_tuning', default=...) here and DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT in src/sentry/constants.py:724 — and this PR had to edit both in lockstep to move 'low' to 'off'. The next change to this default will edit one file and not the other, silently diverging the project-option default from the constants-level default; registering the option with the constant would leave a single place to update.

[BUG] get_environment_info() and get_merged_pr_single_issue_template() interpolate the unescaped issue title and event-derived environment name into the markdown PR-comment template, and the new template `* ‼️ [**{title}**]({url}){environment}` places the attacker-controlled title inside the link-text position for the first time. Both values come from event data that anyone who can send events to the project's DSN controls (the environment name and the error title are client-supplied, not org-member-supplied). A title like `x](https://evil.com)` closes the markdown link early so the rendered comment links attacker-chosen text to an attacker URL, and an environment name containing backticks (e.g. `` a` in `b](https://evil.com) ``) breaks out of the code-span wrapper in get_environment_info's `f" in `{environment.name}`"` return. The result is attacker-crafted links (and potential @mention pings) injected into comments the Sentry bot posts on GitHub/GitLab PRs via GitHubPRCommentWorkflow/GitlabPRCommentWorkflow get_comment_body — a phishing vector that did not exist in the old template, where the link text was the static string 'View Issue' and the target was always the Sentry URL.

[BUG] The new owner field uses ActorField, which validates only that the referenced user/team exists globally (no organization-membership check anywhere in this validator), and both the update path (lines 65-79) and the create path write owner.id straight into owner_user_id/owner_team_id. A user with detector-edit permission in organization A can set a detector's owner to any user ID or team ID in the entire installation, including teams that belong to other organizations, because ActorField's existence check queries User/Team without an org filter and the diff adds no org-scoped validation before persisting the IDs. The existence-vs-nonexistence validation error also doubles as a global user/team ID enumeration oracle for org-level editors. Downstream consumers that resolve detector owner (ownership display and any notification/assignment routing built on detector owner) then operate on entities outside the org's membership.

[BUG] BrowserReportSerializer validates `url` with serializers.URLField(), which only accepts http/https/ftp/ftps hierarchical URLs, so reports whose page URL is e.g. `about:blank` or `chrome-error://chromewebdata` fail is_valid(), and the POST loop returns 422 on the first invalid report, dropping the entire batch. Browser Reporting API deliveries that the previous dataclass path accepted and counted (any string URL/type) are now rejected wholesale: none of the reports in an affected payload are counted in browser_reporting.raw_report_received, and the browser sees the whole delivery fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Both age and timestamp are declared required=False and neither validate_timestamp nor validate_age runs when both are absent, so a report containing neither field passes validation although both supported Reporting API specs require one of them. Malformed or hostile clients (the endpoint is CSRF-exempt and CORS-open) receive 200s for reports neither spec can produce, and the raw_report_received metric counts garbage as if it were real browser telemetry.

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportSerializer` (src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py), both `age` and `timestamp` are `required=False`. The only checks are in `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age`, which run only if their respective field is present. Therefore a report payload with neither `age` nor `timestamp` will pass `serializer.is_valid()` and be accepted (200) and counted in `metrics.incr(...)`. The diff adds no object-level `validate()` enforcing “exactly one of age/timestamp must be present”, and tests only cover the mixed-fields case, not the missing-both case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion checks test truthiness (self.initial_data.get("age") / self.initial_data.get("timestamp")) instead of key presence, so a report carrying both timestamp and age=0 (or age with timestamp=0) validates despite the contract the docstrings state. Contradictory reports that the validators explicitly promise to reject are accepted and counted; the exclusion invariant only holds for truthy values, so the enforcement is weaker than the documented contract.

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportSerializer` (added in `browser_reporting_collector.py`), `validate_timestamp` checks `if self.initial_data.get("age")` and `validate_age` checks `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`. These are truthiness checks, not key-presence checks. Because `age` is an `IntegerField(required=False)` (no `min_value`) and `timestamp` allows `0` (`min_value=0`), payloads containing both fields with one set to `0` (e.g. `age: 0` with a `timestamp`, or `timestamp: 0` with an `age`) will not trigger either validation error, violating the mutual-exclusion contract stated in the docstrings and allowing contradictory reports to be accepted and counted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] url is now serializers.URLField(), whose validator only accepts http/https/ftp/ftps URLs with a // authority, replacing the previous accept-anything str field with no allowance for the non-http document URIs the Reporting API permits. Real reports with non-http document URLs — e.g. CSP-violation reports from about:blank/data: sandboxed frames or extension/error pages — now fail validation and return 422, silently dropping them from the browser_reporting metrics this endpoint exists to collect.

adjudication.rationale: In `browser_reporting_collector.py`, the `url` field changed from an unvalidated string in the old `BrowserReport` dataclass (`url: str`) to `BrowserReportSerializer.url = serializers.URLField()`. DRF's `URLField` enforces a standard URL format (and typically only allows common schemes like http/https/ftp with proper structure), which will reject valid Reporting API `url` values such as `about:blank`, `data:` URLs, extension URLs, etc. With the new per-report validation, any such report will cause `.is_valid()` to fail and the endpoint returns `HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY`, meaning those reports will not reach the metrics increment loop (`metrics.incr(...)`) and will be effectively dropped for the metric this endpoint is meant to collect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] update() reads validated_data.get("detector_type", instance.group_type) but the serializer's field is type (create() reads validated_data["type"]), so the detector_type key is never present and every update re-assigns instance.type from the existing group_type. PATCH requests that attempt to change a detector's type return 200 while the type is silently left unchanged — the caller's edit is dropped without any error, and the two methods bind two different names for the same validated_data key.
matched_golden_ids: In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that update() incorrectly looks up `validated_data['detector_type']` even though the serializer field/key is `type` (as used in create()), causing type changes to be ignored. This is the same underlying bug as the golden comment (wrong key used when updating `instance.type`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The owner-resolution logic (is_user/is_team branching into owner_user_id/owner_team_id) is duplicated between create() and update() with already-divergent shapes: update() explicitly clears the opposite field in each branch while create() relies on None initialization. The next owner-rule change (e.g. restricting owners to teams) must be applied in two structurally different blocks; a fix landed in one silently misses the other, and the divergence visible today shows this drift has already started.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/workflow_engine/endpoints/validators/base/detector.py`, the owner-to-fields mapping is implemented twice: once in `update()` (explicitly setting/clearing `instance.owner_user_id` vs `instance.owner_team_id`) and once in `create()` (deriving `owner_user_id`/`owner_team_id` local vars before `Detector.objects.create(...)`). While this isn’t a functional defect in the diff (create initializes both to `None` so the “other” field is effectively cleared for a new row), it is a real maintenance/architecture issue grounded in the diff: any future rule change for owner handling would need to be made in two different code blocks and could easily drift.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] CommitContextIntegration.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template reaches into PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title, coupling the integration base class to the comment-workflow class hierarchy for a helper that belongs beside ISSUE_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH and the template constant it serves. Title-truncation policy now lives in one class while its constant and its only new caller live in another, so the next truncation change must touch two layers — and the cross-class reference is a latent NameError if the module graph between integrations and the workflow classes changes.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py`, the newly added `CommitContextIntegration.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template()` calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)` even though a `_truncate_title` helper is defined alongside it on `CommitContextIntegration`. It’s also fragile in that it relies on `PRCommentWorkflow` being present in this module’s globals and having/inheriting `_truncate_title`, rather than using the local helper (`CommitContextIntegration._truncate_title` or `self._truncate_title`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Removing the regex-experiment branch leaves the module-level _handle_regex_match helper with no remaining caller in the dispatcher, while the ParameterizationRegex base class it was written for still exists with its different callback contract. The next editor sees two live-looking callback contracts (the dead re.Match helper and the active (str, int) counter) and can bind the wrong one when touching this dispatcher; the orphaned helper should be deleted together with the experiment class it served.

adjudication.rationale: In src/sentry/grouping/parameterization.py the diff removes ParameterizationRegexExperiment and the isinstance-based dispatcher branch, and narrows ParameterizationExperiment to only ParameterizationCallableExperiment. However, inside the dispatcher method a helper `def _handle_regex_match(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:` is still present, even though the only remaining call site was the removed `else: content = experiment.run(content, _handle_regex_match)`. This is not a runtime defect today (it’s just dead code), but it is a concrete cleanup/maintainability issue introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new processing_deadline_duration values (30 here, 300 on drain_mailbox at ~line 161, 120 on drain_mailbox_parallel at ~line 239) are bare literals with no stated unit rationale or provenance, and drain_mailbox performs external HTTP deliveries whose duration directly determines whether the deadline fires. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] processing_deadline_duration=60 is a bare literal with no stated provenance on the check_auth_identities sweep task. If the identity sweep's worst-case duration exceeds 60s the task is killed and redelivered mid-sweep, reprocessing identities; nothing in the code records why 60 is safe for a sweep whose input size grows with the auth-identity table.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `check_auth_identities` in `src/sentry/tasks/auth/check_auth.py` to set `TaskworkerConfig(namespace=auth_control_tasks, processing_deadline_duration=60)`. The finding correctly notes this is a hard-coded literal with no explanation in the diff. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble") fires before the organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble feature check and before any request-body validation. Requests that are subsequently rejected with 404 (feature disabled) or 4xx (invalid payload) are counted as assemble events, so anyone reading this analytics stream to measure feature adoption or API usage gets inflated numbers that include rejected traffic.
matched_golden_ids: Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue describes analytics being recorded before the feature-flag check, causing events to be logged even when the request later returns 404 due to the feature being disabled, inflating/misleading analytics—same core issue as the golden comment (it also adds invalid-payload cases, but that’s consistent/extra detail).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT flips "low" to "off" in lockstep with the second copy of the same default in projectoptions/defaults.py (sentry:autofix_automation_tuning, line 205), silently changing effective behavior for every organization without an explicit option value. adjudication.rationale: The diff does verifiably change the default autofix automation tuning from "low" to "off" in two places: `src/sentry/constants.py` (`DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT`) and `src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py` (`register(key="sentry:autofix_automation_tuning", default="off")`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Report handling changed from per-report counting to all-or-nothing validation: the loop returns 422 on the first invalid report before any metrics.incr runs, so valid reports sharing a payload with one invalid report are no longer counted at all (the old loop counted each report as it parsed it). Sentry's browser-reporting metrics undercount whenever a browser sends a batch containing any malformed report; per the Reporting API the browser re-sends the batch, so a deterministically-invalid report poisons every retry until the attempt limit is reached, permanently discarding the counts of the valid reports in those batches.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes browser report handling to “all-or-nothing” validation: in `BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint.post`, each report is validated in a first pass and the handler `return`s a 422 immediately on the first invalid report (`if not serializer.is_valid(): ... return Response(..., 422)`), before any `metrics.incr(...)` calls. Only after all reports validate does it loop again to increment metrics. Previously, metrics were incremented inline per-report (`for report in raw_data: BrowserReport(**report); metrics.incr(...)`), so earlier valid reports in the batch could be counted before a later failure. Whether this is a defect is product/semantics-dependent (422 implies rejecting the whole request), but the behavioral/metering change is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion check uses truthiness on initial_data and only runs when a field is present, so a report carrying neither age nor timestamp validates successfully, and a report with timestamp plus age=0 (or age plus timestamp=0) bypasses the exclusion check these validators exist to enforce. Reports that satisfy neither W3C draft (no age and no timestamp) are accepted and counted, and spec-violating reports carrying both fields with a 0 value slip through, polluting exactly the browser-reporting dataset this rewrite was meant to tighten.

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportSerializer` (src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py), both `age` and `timestamp` are `required=False`, and the mutual-exclusion logic is implemented only in `validate_timestamp` / `validate_age`. Those validators are only invoked if the corresponding field is present, so a report containing neither `age` nor `timestamp` will validate successfully. Additionally, both validators use truthiness checks (`self.initial_data.get("age")` / `get("timestamp")`), so a payload containing both fields with zero values (`age: 0` and `timestamp: 0`) would bypass the exclusion checks (0 is falsy) and validate, despite violating the intended “support both specs but not both fields” constraint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The snuba query_replay_instance call that produces error_ids runs unconditionally before the enable_error_context check, so the disable flag only skips the nodestore fetch and never avoids the remote query it exists to turn off. Callers that pass enable_error_context=false to avoid the error-context cost still pay a full snuba query on every summarize request, so the opt-out knob added for cost control does not control the dominant added cost on this path.

adjudication.rationale: In `ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get` (src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py), the code performs `query_replay_instance(...)` and `process_raw_response(...)` to compute `error_ids` before evaluating `enable_error_context` (stored as `disable_error_fetching`). Even when `enable_error_context=false`, the Snuba query still runs and only the subsequent nodestore fetch is skipped. So the flag does not prevent the added remote query cost introduced by this change, which is a concrete performance/cost-control concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Error-context extraction is coupled to client-supplied query parameters: process_raw_response filters rows to request.query_params.getlist('field'), so error_ids is empty unless the caller explicitly includes field=error_ids, and the new feature silently no-ops otherwise. Any summarize caller whose field list omits error_ids (older frontend builds during deploy skew, API consumers) gets summaries with no error context and no error or log explaining why, making the capability appear randomly broken instead of failing loudly.

adjudication.rationale: In `ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get`, error context is derived from `error_ids` extracted after `process_raw_response(snuba_response, fields=request.query_params.getlist('field'))` and then `response[0].get('error_ids', [])` (new code in `src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`). Because the post-processing is explicitly parameterized by the client-provided `field` list, this creates a coupling where the presence of `error_ids` in the processed response may depend on whether the caller requested that field. The diff does not show `process_raw_response` internals, so it's not provable that `error_ids` will be dropped, but the endpoint now risks silently omitting error context for callers that don’t include `field=error_ids`, with no explicit fallback or logging.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] fetch_error_details and gen_request_data inject every error of the replay into the Seer prompt with no cap on error_ids — a replay with hundreds of errors produces hundreds of nodestore fetches and an unbounded list of 'User experienced an error: ...' lines in the LLM request. Error-heavy replays drive per-request nodestore/snuba cost and Seer prompt size with no ceiling; an oversized Seer request surfaces as response.raise_for_status() raising inside on_results, turning the summarize request into a 500 for exactly the replays with the most errors.

adjudication.rationale: In `project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`, the new logic pulls `error_ids` from the Snuba replay instance response (`error_ids = response[0].get("error_ids", [])`) and passes them to `fetch_error_details` with no cap/limit. `fetch_error_details` builds node IDs for every error and calls `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)`, then `gen_request_data` interleaves *all* error messages into the `logs` list sent to Seer (`json.dumps({"logs": get_request_data(...)})`). The finding is correct that prompt size and nodestore work are unbounded by this diff and could cause performance/robustness issues for error-heavy replays. However, the claim of "hundreds of nodestore fetches" is slightly overstated since the code uses a single `get_multi` call rather than per-error fetches, and the 500-on-oversize behavior is plausible but not strictly proven from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE ends with a literal \n while both the GitHub and GitLab call sites still assemble the list with "\n".join(...), producing a blank line between every issue entry plus a trailing blank line, where the previous template produced a single-spaced list. Merged-PR comments posted to GitHub and GitLab render as a double-spaced issue list with a trailing empty line — a user-visible formatting regression introduced incidentally by the template move rather than a deliberate layout change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE = "* ‼️ [**{title}**]({url}){environment}\n"` in `commit_context.py`, and both GitHub/GitLab workflows still build `issue_list` via `"\n".join([...])`, so each entry contributes its own trailing newline plus the join separator, producing blank lines between items and a trailing newline. However, the PR also updates the expected comment bodies in tests to include these blank lines, suggesting the spacing is now intended/accepted rather than a clearly unintended correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] analytics.record('preprod_artifact.api.assemble', ...) fires at the top of post() before the organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble feature check, so requests that are immediately rejected with 403 are recorded as assemble API usage. Adoption and funnel metrics for the preprod assemble API are inflated by denied traffic from organizations that never had the feature, skewing the product decisions this analytics event is meant to inform.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/preprod/api/endpoints/organization_preprod_artifact_assemble.py`, the diff adds `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` at the very start of `post()` (before the `features.has("organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble", ...)` gate). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The autofix automation default exists as two hand-synced literals — register(key='sentry:autofix_automation_tuning', default=...) here and DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT in src/sentry/constants.py:724 — and this PR had to edit both in lockstep to move 'low' to 'off'. The next change to this default will edit one file and not the other, silently diverging the project-option default from the constants-level default; registering the option with the constant would leave a single place to update.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] get_environment_info() and get_merged_pr_single_issue_template() interpolate the unescaped issue title and event-derived environment name into the markdown PR-comment template, and the new template `* ‼️ [**{title}**]({url}){environment}` places the attacker-controlled title inside the link-text position for the first time. Both values come from event data that anyone who can send events to the project's DSN controls (the environment name and the error title are client-supplied, not org-member-supplied). A title like `x](https://evil.com)` closes the markdown link early so the rendered comment links attacker-chosen text to an attacker URL, and an environment name containing backticks (e.g. `` a` in `b](https://evil.com) ``) breaks out of the code-span wrapper in get_environment_info's `f" in `{environment.name}`"` return. The result is attacker-crafted links (and potential @mention pings) injected into comments the Sentry bot posts on GitHub/GitLab PRs via GitHubPRCommentWorkflow/GitlabPRCommentWorkflow get_comment_body — a phishing vector that did not exist in the old template, where the link text was the static string 'View Issue' and the target was always the Sentry URL.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new markdown template for PR comments in `src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py`: `MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE = "* ‼️ [**{title}**]({url}){environment}\n"`. `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template()` formats this with `title=issue.title` (only truncated via `_truncate_title`, not escaped) and `environment=self.get_environment_info(issue)`. `get_environment_info()` pulls `environment.name` from `issue.get_recommended_event().get_environment()` and returns `f" in `{environment.name}`"` without escaping backticks or other markdown metacharacters. Both `issue.title` and `environment.name` are derived from event data (the tests explicitly set event `environment`), so they can contain markdown control characters. Because the title is now placed inside link-text delimiters `[...]`, crafted values containing `](` or backticks can break out and inject attacker-controlled markdown (links/mentions) into GitHub/GitLab bot comments.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new owner field uses ActorField, which validates only that the referenced user/team exists globally (no organization-membership check anywhere in this validator), and both the update path (lines 65-79) and the create path write owner.id straight into owner_user_id/owner_team_id. A user with detector-edit permission in organization A can set a detector's owner to any user ID or team ID in the entire installation, including teams that belong to other organizations, because ActorField's existence check queries User/Team without an org filter and the diff adds no org-scoped validation before persisting the IDs. The existence-vs-nonexistence validation error also doubles as a global user/team ID enumeration oracle for org-level editors. Downstream consumers that resolve detector owner (ownership display and any notification/assignment routing built on detector owner) then operate on entities outside the org's membership.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `owner = ActorField(required=False, allow_null=True)` and persists `owner.id` into `owner_user_id`/`owner_team_id` on create/update, but the finding’s core claim (no org-scoped validation, allowing cross-org user/team ownership and ID enumeration) is contradicted by new endpoint tests in the same diff. `tests/sentry/workflow_engine/endpoints/test_organization_detector_index.py::test_owner_not_in_organization` explicitly sets `owner` to a user from another organization and asserts a 400 with an `owner` error, demonstrating that cross-org owners are rejected somewhere in the request validation pipeline. Since the diff shows this behavior is enforced, the claimed vulnerability is not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] BrowserReportSerializer validates `url` with serializers.URLField(), which only accepts http/https/ftp/ftps hierarchical URLs, so reports whose page URL is e.g. `about:blank` or `chrome-error://chromewebdata` fail is_valid(), and the POST loop returns 422 on the first invalid report, dropping the entire batch. Browser Reporting API deliveries that the previous dataclass path accepted and counted (any string URL/type) are now rejected wholesale: none of the reports in an affected payload are counted in browser_reporting.raw_report_received, and the browser sees the whole delivery fail.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py`, the new `BrowserReportSerializer` uses `url = serializers.URLField()`, which enforces DRF’s URL validation (typically only hierarchical URLs with schemes like http/https/ftp/ftps). The previous implementation (`BrowserReport` dataclass) accepted `url` as an arbitrary string with no validation. The new POST handler also returns `422` immediately on the first invalid report (`if not serializer.is_valid(): ... return Response(..., 422)`), so a single report with a non-URLField-acceptable URL (e.g. `about:blank`, `chrome-error://...`) will cause the entire batch to be rejected and *none* of the metrics in `browser_reporting.raw_report_received` will be incremented for otherwise-valid reports in the payload. This is a behavior regression and can lead to dropped batches.

However, the finding’s stronger claim about the merged-PR path only working under an inheritance relationship (vs composition) is not verifiable from this diff because the definitions/relationships of `PRCommentWorkflow` and how workflows delegate to the integration are not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] query_replay_instance (Snuba) runs unconditionally on every GET even when enable_error_context=false, whose only effect is skipping the nodestore fetch — the query result (error_ids) is computed and then discarded. Callers using the documented disable knob to avoid the added error-context work still pay a Snuba query on every request, and the query re-runs for every pagination offset because it sits before self.paginate.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] fetch_error_details pairs error_ids with nodestore get_multi(...).values() via zip, but get_multi omits nodes that are missing or undecodable (per the NodeStorage contract), so any absent event shifts every subsequent id-to-data pairing by one. When any error event is absent from nodestore (expired/evicted) or error_ids contains a duplicate that the dict collapses, each later error_id is paired with the wrong event's title/message/timestamp and the endpoint returns 200 with a Seer summary that misattributes errors, with no error surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`, `fetch_error_details` does `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` and then builds results with `for event_id, data in zip(error_ids, events.values())`. This assumes `events.values()` is positionally aligned with `error_ids`, but `get_multi` returns a dict keyed by node_id (so duplicates in `error_ids`/`node_ids` necessarily collapse to a single entry) and may also omit missing entries. Either case changes the length/order of `events.values()`, causing later `event_id`s to be paired with the wrong `data` (misattributed titles/messages/timestamps) rather than being skipped.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] fetch_error_details catches every exception and returns [], so the summarize endpoint returns 200 both when the replay has no errors and when the nodestore fetch failed. A nodestore outage silently degrades every generated summary (error context missing) and the degradation is indistinguishable from 'replay had zero errors' for the user; only a generic Sentry capture distinguishes them, with no metric on the degradation path.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`, `fetch_error_details()` wraps the nodestore fetch in a broad `except Exception` and on failure does `sentry_sdk.capture_exception(e)` then returns `[]`. The endpoint then proceeds normally and still paginates/returns 200 with summaries generated from breadcrumbs only (since `analyze_recording_segments` is called with `error_events` and will just omit error log lines when the list is empty). This makes a nodestore outage (or other fetch failure) indistinguishable from the legitimate case where `error_ids` is empty / replay has no errors, and the diff adds no metric/log specifically for this degradation path beyond a generic exception capture.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] validate_timestamp and validate_age test the sibling field with truthiness (self.initial_data.get('age') / .get('timestamp')) instead of presence checks, so a report carrying both age and timestamp is accepted when both values are 0, and a report carrying neither field is accepted. Reports that violate the mutual-exclusion rule the validators' own error messages assert pass validation and are counted in metrics with no usable time information, instead of being rejected with 422.
matched_golden_ids: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same root bug: the validators use truthiness via self.initial_data.get('age') / .get('timestamp'), so zero values are treated as missing. This breaks the mutual-exclusion/presence logic, allowing invalid combinations (e.g., both age=0 and timestamp=0, or neither) to pass. The golden specifically calls out checking key presence ('timestamp' in self.initial_data), which is the same fix direction the candidate implies (presence checks).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] url = serializers.URLField() rejects URL strings browsers legitimately send (e.g. 'about:blank' for opaque origins, 'blob:...' worker URLs), where the previous implementation accepted any string. Batches containing reports from sandboxed iframes or blob workers are rejected with 422 and re-attempted by the browser until attempts are exhausted, silently dropping reports the collector previously counted.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py` the new `BrowserReportSerializer` changes `url` from an unvalidated `str` (previously `BrowserReport.url: str` constructed via `BrowserReport(**report)`) to `serializers.URLField()`. DRF/Django URL validation is scheme-restrictive (typically http/https/ftp/ftps) and will reject nonstandard-but-real schemes like `about:` or `blob:`. This means a batch containing such reports will now fail `serializer.is_valid()` and return 422 (`HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY`), whereas the previous implementation would have accepted and counted them. That is a behavior-breaking change consistent with the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The validation loop returns on the first invalid report, so a single malformed report causes the entire browser batch (including all valid reports) to be rejected. One bad report in a batch of N drops N-1 valid reports and drives browser retry amplification against the collector until the offending report ages out of the browser's buffer.

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint.post`, each report is validated in a loop and on the first invalid report the code immediately `return Response(..., status=HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY)` (see the `if not serializer.is_valid(): ... return Response(...)` inside the `for report in raw_data:` loop). This makes the endpoint all-or-nothing for batched reports: any single malformed entry prevents processing/metric recording for the rest of the batch. Whether this is a "bug" depends on intended API semantics (batch atomicity vs partial acceptance), but the finding is accurately grounded in the diff and highlights a real operational concern introduced by the chosen control flow.
